newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks seen firming amid positive sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks seen firming amid positive sentiment.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are expected to gain ground on Friday as participants should be encouraged by the firmness in New York stocks and the yen's retreat against the dollar overnight, brokers said.
But trading is still likely to be thin as many participants are away for summer vacations, they said.
On Thursday, the Nikkei 225 average finished 214.02 points or 1.13 percent higher at 19,222.62. September futures gained 250 points to 19,280.
"Market sentiment will be relatively positive as New York stocks ended firmer and the yen declined against the dollar last night," said Yasuo Ueki, general manager at Nikko Securities.
He also said that public pension funds are inclined to bargain hunt when the Nikkei index falls below 19,000, supporting share prices at the downside.
Brokers said, however, some dealers may sell to adjust their long positions ahead of the weekend.
Japan's chip equipment makers jumped on Thursday, encouraged by a surge in shares of U.S. chip equipment maker Applied Materials Inc on Wednesday, brokers said.
Turnover on the Tokyo bourse's first section was a modest 202 million shares by midday, against 170 million shares traded by Thursday midday.
Gainers outpaced losers 576 to 423, while 190 issues were unchanged.
The broader TOPIX index nudged up 12.46 points, or 0.83 percent, to 1,507.15. The Nikkei 300 average was up 2.96 points, or 1.01 percent, at 295.55.

Among high-tech shares, Pioneer Electronic Corp, an audio equipment maker, jumped 310 yen or 12.16 percent to 2,860 yen, making it the second-largest percentage gainer on the Tokyo bourse's first section.
Brokers said the shares attracted buying due to expectations of a positive earnings report on Monday.
Semiconductor equipment maker Nikon Corp rose 150 yen to 2,660 yen and Tokyo Electron Ltd gained 250 yen to 7,900 yen, both hitting all-time highs.
On the losers' side, shares of Towa Real Estate Development Co Ltd, a real estate developer, plunged.

The shares shed 49 yen or 37.40 percent to end the morning at a record low of 82 yen, topping the list of percentage losers on the bourse's first section, while its trading volume, at 5.192 million, was the second-heaviest.
Towa's shares were hit by rumours that it is experiencing business difficulties. Officials at the firm were not available to comments on the rumours, due to a company holiday.

Shares in Fujita Corp, Towa's parent, also declined, shedding 16 yen or 15.24 percent to 89 yen, making it the third-largest percentage loser. It was also the most actively traded issue, with turnover of 10.23 million shares.
By sector, gainers were led by rubber, miscellaneous manufacturers, warehousing, pulp/paper, and precision instruments. The major losers were shipbuilding, gas, construction, oil, and land transport.
